faq.q: Can I read fuel level remotely on a Hyundai Bayon?
faq.a: Yes, with a DIMO device, which reports Fuel Percentage as the powertrainFuelSystemRelativeLevel signal. Once the owner shares the vehicle, exchange your Developer JWT for a Vehicle JWT and query the signal through the Telemetry API.

faq.q: How do I track a Hyundai Bayon with no connected services?
faq.a: Use a DIMO device. After the owner shares the vehicle with your Developer License, request a Vehicle JWT from the Token Exchange API and use it with the Telemetry API to read the vehicle's data.

faq.q: How do I detect idling on a Hyundai Bayon?
faq.a: Query the segments resource in the Telemetry API with the idling mechanism, which requires a DIMO device. Segments are contiguous periods where engine RPM stays in the idle range, and you can adjust the upper bound with maxIdleRpm (default 1000).

faq.q: How do I detect refuel events on a Hyundai Bayon?
faq.a: Query segments with the refuel mechanism, which detects where fuel level rises significantly. The minIncreasePercent setting controls the minimum rise, with a default of 15 percent.

faq.q: How do I verify Hyundai Bayon mileage?
faq.a: The DIMO device reports the odometer signal. To get verifiable proof of it, call the Attestation API odometer-statement endpoint with a Vehicle JWT, then retrieve the resulting credential through the Telemetry API.

intro: DIMO gives developers API access to vehicle-state data: diagnostics, fault codes, battery and fuel health, odometer, and maintenance signals. For the Hyundai Bayon, that data comes through a DIMO device on model years 2023 and newer, and this coverage has been tested rather than only expected. Vehicle owners consent to and control sharing, so builders get data with clear provenance. DIMO adds vehicle-state depth on top of GPS tracking; it doesn't replace it.
